title: Hamiltonian Asymmetric Fusion: One-Way Safe Directed Refinement under Modality Imbalance
claim: Prior fusion mixes information symmetrically in both directions; ours refines only the weaker stream, guided one-way by the stronger one.
layout: 2 stacked panels, left-to-right flow, shared legend box at bottom
description: Two stacked block diagrams share one color-coded legend at the bottom. The top panel shows the prior CDA block. A yellow primary stream (circles) and a green auxiliary stream (triangles) enter Norm and self-attention (SA) boxes. They are then cross-mixed inside a teal rounded region through matrices, multiplication nodes and a summation node. The outputs are concatenated (A), added back, and passed through Norm and FFN. The bottom panel shows the proposed HAF block. Its pink rounded region holds spectral global correlation (SGC) inputs, a force/gate diamond, and two p/q momentum refinement loops. Only the weaker stream's path is refined. It returns with 'strong' and 'weak' labels, followed by concatenation, Norm and FFN. Yellow and green arrows trace each stream. The eye goes first to the two colored background blobs, CDA and HAF.
caption: Comparison between CDA and HAF. Top: CDA performs symmetric cross-diffusion by mutually propagating information
abstract: In RGB--D salient object detection, multimodal fusion is commonly implemented via symmetric token interaction, implicitly allowing information to flow in both directions. Under modality imbalance ---when an auxiliary stream is substantially noisier than a designated primary stream---such symmetry creates a backflow channel that injects auxiliary noise into the primary representation and amplifies errors across iterative refinement stages. We formulate fusion in this regime as directed refinement with one-way safety : the primary modality defines a guidance field, while only auxiliary representations are iteratively purified, and primary perturbations induced by the auxiliary stream are explicitly bounded. We propose Hamiltonian Asymmetric Fusion (HAF), a lightweight unrolled refinement block that updates auxiliary tokens with momentum regularization and gated driving. The refinement force is instantiated by FFT-based spectral global correlation and modulated by a shared learnable spectral response to emphasize reliable frequency components with minimal parameters; a leaky momentum gate and a stable integrator improve multi-step refinement stability. We provide guarantees of auxiliary error contraction and bounded primary perturbation, which symmetric fusion operators do not satisfy under imbalance. Experiments on six RGB--D SOD benchmarks show consistent gains and substantially more graceful degradation under controlled auxiliary corruption.
